value: in situ in a cave pool, cavefish-like fish spent on average 24 s in the fish-food-extract-infused area versus 1.8 s in the control area during a 1-min test (P < 0.01)
units: seconds in area during a 1-min test
method: in situ field olfactory test: fish held 48 h in an inflatable pool beside the cave, then fish-food extract delivered through an odorant tube in one corner and a control solution in another; time in the extract-infused versus the control area scored over the first minute
conditions: nine fish trapped overnight with a meat-baited minnow trap in the second pool of the Rio Subterraneo cave (Sierra de El Abra region, San Luis Potosi, Mexico), March 2013 dry season, comprising eyed and eyeless phenotypes sorted by eye size into 5 cavefish-like (CF-like) and 4 surface-fish-like (SF-like) fish (Figure 2 legend: CF-like = 5, SF-like = 4); extract made from 5 g of granular fish food (TetraDiskus) in 50 ml of local water, filtered through glass microfibre filters, no concentration stated; test pool 61 x 61 x 15 cm; error bars are standard deviations

source.authors: Bibliowicz J, Alie A, Espinasa L, Yoshizawa M, Blin M, Hinaux H, Legendre L, Pere S, Retaux S
source.title: Differences in chemosensory response between eyed and eyeless Astyanax mexicanus of the Rio Subterráneo cave

quote: They spent an average of 24 s in the extract-infused area, which was significantly more than the 1.8 s spent in the control area during the 1-min test (P < 0.01) (Figure 2D).
note: Classification: behavioural response of wild-caught cave fish to a food odour; no chemoreceptor is identified. The sentence is the second of two (the first, 'Although at any given time a few of the CF-like fish came at the extract-infused corner, each of them approached the odorant tube at some point during the test.'); 'They' are the CF-like fish. Contrary and secondary results from the same paper: 'none of the SF-like fish approached the food extract corner throughout the test (P < 0.01 compared with CF-like fish)' (SF-like n = 4); naris size was 'significantly larger' in CF-like than SF-like individuals (Figure 3 legend n = 4, P < 0.01, adjusted to body length). Design limits: the groups are phenotype classes of one wild population, not sexes or lines; n is 5 and 4 fish; the extract and control stimuli are not matched in concentration (none stated) and no statistical test name is printed in the sentence (the Methods print 'A Mann–Whitney U test was utilized to determine the statistical significance of the results.'); the extract is a commercial fish food, not a natural odour; fish were held 48 h in captivity before testing. value: tadpoles swam less in water with rough-skinned newt (Taricha granulosa) cue than in control water (Tukey post-hoc p = 0.05)
method: laboratory single-tadpole trials: 2 mL of newt-soaked water (adult newts soaked 2 h in 300 mL aged tap water) or aged tap water control added to a container of 200 mL aged tap water; 2 min acclimation then 10 min scored for Nothing, Foraging, Swimming and Frantic Swimming
conditions: 90 trials with 17 tadpoles (31 newt cue, 31 control, 28 invasive Xenopus laevis cue) tested 25 May to 22 June 2022 at Gosner stages 24-42; two partial egg masses (about 50 embryos each) collected 24 March 2022 from a stormwater pond in Washington state, hatched and held individually in 0.47 L containers on ground fish flakes; the Methods also say tadpoles were collected from an adjacent pond, which does not clearly match the egg-mass account; tadpoles were assigned treatments so each experienced different treatments in successive trials, no randomised order is described; trials are repeated measures on the same 17 tadpoles; cue concentration not measured; models included tadpole identity and day-of-year as random effects; newts were wild-collected and held captive at least two weeks before trials per Methods (the Discussion says 1-2 months); no sample size printed in the Results sentence

source.title: Feral frogs, native newts, and chemical cues: identifying threats from and management opportunities for invasive African Clawed Frogs in Washington state

quote: Tukey's post-hoc tests found that R. aurora tadpole Swimming rates were reduced in the newt treatment compared to Control treatments (p= 0.05).
note: Classification: behavioural response of tadpoles reared from wild-collected eggs to a predator-soaked-water cue; no chemoreceptor is identified and the effect sits at the p = 0.05 threshold. Nulls and secondary results from the same paper: the overall model found differences in R. aurora behaviour (p = 0.03); Swimming in the invasive X. laevis cue treatment did not differ from control (p = 0.87) or from the newt treatment (p = 0.15); the Results sentence prints a curly apostrophe in 'Tukey’s', straightened here; Frantic Swimming (p = 0.09) and Foraging (p = 0.89) showed no treatment difference; the Discussion says tadpoles decreased Foraging and increased Frantic Swimming under newt cues, which the Results statistics do not support.
